chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from one of his companions, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the child who steals, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is nine years of age, his hand is cut, and a penalty (hadd) from the penalties of Allah (Exalted and Glorious) is not wasted.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on cutting the hand of a child who steals according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the age of nine is the threshold for applying the hadd of theft, distinguishing it from general criminal liability. This ruling underscores the principle that the divine penalty is not nullified by the perpetrator's youth, provided they have reached the age of discernment (tamyiz). It reflects the Shia juristic view that the hadd is a right of God that must be executed once the specific conditions of age and capacity are met.
